subject.title: fix(release): keep reviewed migration residue nonfatal

question: Should release/2026.7.1 treat these two retained-but-reviewed migration residues as nonfatal notices, following the policy established by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102780, while keeping ambiguous ownership, canonical-state mutation, and I/O failures blocking?
rationale: The choice determines upgrade-time persisted-state handling and whether the gateway fails closed, so automation cannot safely decide the availability and compatibility policy despite the patch's strong implementation and proof.

options.title: Accept the narrow residue policy
options.body: Land the PR because canonical SQLite remains authoritative, foreign-harness state remains untouched, operator visibility is preserved, and true failures still block readiness.

options.title: Require cleanup convergence
options.body: Request archiving or removal that makes the artifacts disappear before allowing startup, rather than retaining them indefinitely as notices.

options.title: Pause for unified migration policy
options.body: Hold the release change until maintainers choose one policy covering all remaining residue families in the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow residue policy
recommendation.body: Land the PR because canonical SQLite remains authoritative, foreign-harness state remains untouched, operator visibility is preserved, and true failures still block readiness.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue is assigned to vincentkoc, and their recent history covers the central state-migration and SQLite conflict paths.
